ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014; Executive Regulations of the Anti-Money Laundering Law issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 95 of 2004, as amended; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT directives and circulars; Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (Egyptian FIU) implementing decisions; and the applicable provisions of Law No. 72 of 2017 on Investment and GAFI's Beneficial Ownership Register implementation rules.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, shareholders, signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners must undergo mandatory screening against the UN Security Council Sanctions List, the U.S. OFAC SDN List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the Egyptian Terrorist Entities and Terrorist Financing List administered by the Egyptian Ministry of Justice, and the domestic PEP register maintained by Egyptian law enforcement/financial intelligence authorities. Enhanced Due Diligence applies to any individual identified as a PEP, any entity incorporated in or receiving revenue from a sanctioned jurisdiction, and any transaction involving foreign politically exposed persons. Ongoing risk-based monitoring is required after incorporation, and updated screening must be performed at least every 30 days during the pre-incorporation phase.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Egyptian General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Online Services / E-Services corporate registration portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory legal name must be submitted in Arabic; the Arabic form is the controlling identity on the commercial register. A secondary trade name in Latin script may be reserved for cross-border invoicing and payroll SaaS contracts, but the Arabic name always prevails. The chosen name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing company name, trademark, or registered trade name in Egypt, and must not contain religious, national, military, or governmental connotations, or words indicating state affiliation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banking, Money, Financial, Insurance, Re-insurance
Presidential, Government, Ministry, Authority, Federal, Central
Arab Republic of Egypt, Egyptian, Egypt, Cairo, National, Republic
Military, Police, Army, Emblem, Flag, National Shield
Islamic, Sharia, Red Crescent, Red Cross
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name clearance application is rejected, the applicant or incorporation agent may file a written administrative appeal to the GAFI Legal Affairs Department within 15 working days from the date of rejection notice. The appeal must restate the proposed name, attach the rejection decision, and provide legal submissions demonstrating non-conflict with registered names and compliance with Arabic naming rules. A rejected applicant may simultaneously submit an alternative name reservation. Extensions of a valid name reservation are not granted by default; if the incorporation process does not complete within the 30-day reservation window, the applicant must re-file the same name as a new reservation, subject to availability, or choose a new name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office without an in-country physical location is not acceptable as the statutory registered office for an Egyptian LLC. The company must maintain a physical office address in Egypt demonstrated by a lease contract or ownership deed, and the address must be capable of receiving service of process and official correspondence. A serviced business center or co-working location may be used if it provides a dedicated physical occupancy right and a named local office facility, but mail-forwarding-only services will not satisfy the commercial substance requirement for a payroll SaaS platform.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 30-40% within the first 12 months post-incorporation. GAFI may conduct random unannounced visits, and the Egyptian Tax Authority and AML/CFT supervisory authority may also conduct on-site checks to verify economic substance. The likelihood increases if the registered office is shared by multiple newly formed entities or if the company's payroll processing volume signals java high-risk activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Laws No. 4/2020 and No. 185/2020), Articles 102-129 on limited liability companies; Investment Guarantees and Incentives Law No. 72 of 2017; Commercial Code No. 17 of 1999
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), One-Stop Shop, Nasr City / New Cairo, Arabic Republic of Egypt
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association executed before a licensed notary and enrolled with the GAFI One-Stop Shop for issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for LLCs after the 2020 amendments; any capital declared in the Memorandum of Association must be fully subscribed at par and deposited into a temporary escrow bank account opened through the GAFI One-Stop Shop, or fully covered by declared in-kind consideration, before the incorporation certificate is issued
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: one, the Incorporator subscribes in full to the issued share capital of the Company at par per the Memorandum of Association; two, the registered office is fixed at [Registered Address], Cairo, Egypt, and any amendment shall require a board minute; three, the following first officers are appointed until successors are chosen: [Name] as Managing Director, [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] as Company Secretary; four, the Managing Director and Company Secretary are jointly authorized to complete all filings and registrations with GAFI, the Commercial Registry, tax and social insurance authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI E-Service Portal (eserv.gafi.gov.eg) and One-Stop Shop window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed corporate names in priority order through the GAFI electronic name reservation service; each name must include the LLC suffix, avoid restricted or sovereign references, and comply with the Companies Law naming rules. Upon approval, obtain the Name Reservation Certificate valid for sixty days.
required_dossiers: Completed GAFI name reservation application form
Copy of incorporator national ID or passport
Power of attorney if filing through an authorized agent
Publicity search confirmation of name availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the lead name is rejected, the application is automatically queued to the next proposed name; if all three names are rejected, file a new request with revised names and pay only the incremental reservation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of the Memorandum of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian Notary Public and certified corporate attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a bilingual Arabic/English Memorandum of Association through a certified lawyer; all founding members must sign the Arabic original before a notary. The MOA must state the corporate purpose as software development and payroll SaaS platform services under ISIC 6201, the declared share capital, the registered office address within Egypt, and the names and powers of the first managers.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum of Association including corporate purpose clause
Notarized signatures of all founding members
GAFI name reservation certificate
Passport or national ID copies of founding members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Errors in the notarized MOA must be corrected by a supplementary deed executed by all signatories and re-notarized before presentation to GAFI; no new corporate name is required unless the defect concerns the legal name itself.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Application and Escrow Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop, Nasr City / New Cairo
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation file comprising the notarized MOA, the pro-forma first board resolution, the GAFI incorporation form, evidence of paid stamp duty, and the registered office lease. If declared capital is to be paid in cash, open a temporary escrow account at the bank desk inside the One-Stop Shop and deposit the capital before final approval.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum of Association in two originals
Pro-forma first board resolution
Completed GAFI incorporation application form
Receipt of paid statutory stamp duty
Notarized registered office lease or ownership deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query letter, respond within the statutory fifteen-day cure period with corrective documents; a missing declaration can be supplied and the application reactivated without repayment of the full incorporation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office, Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade at the company's domicile
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: GAFI transmits the incorporation record electronically to the competent Commercial Registry; the registry opens the civil commercial file and issues the Certificate of Commercial Registration. Ensure the ISIC 6201 classification and payroll software activity description appear correctly on the certificate.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation certificate
Notarized Memorandum of Association
National ID and criminal record clearance for the general manager
Notarized registered office lease contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry notes an ISIC code mismatch, submit a written amendment request with a certified copy of the MOA and pay the nominal correction fee; the record is adjusted within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Egyptian Tax Authority Registration and Payroll Tax Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), E-TAX Portal and taxpayer services office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register online with the ETA to obtain the Tax Card for corporate income tax and salary/payroll taxes. Apply for VAT registration because SaaS payroll and HR automation subscriptions are taxable services at the standard rate of 14 percent when annual turnover exceeds the VAT registration threshold. Declare the payroll compliance function within the company's own personnel structure.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Commercial Registration
Valid power of attorney for the finance officer
Notarized registered office lease contract
Board resolution appointing the authorized tax representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Tax Card issuance is deferred due to a prior tax ID hold code, lodge a clearance appeal with the ETA taxpayer services office proving absence of prior registrations; a provisional Tax Card may be activated within ten days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI), competent registration office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enroll the LLC as an employer using the Commercial Registration number; declare the opening payroll headcount and remuneration schedule for the quarter in which formation occurs. Open the employer file under the Social Insurance Law to enable lawful payroll automation processing for future staff.
required_dossiers: Completed NOSI employer registration form
Certificate of Commercial Registration
Passport or national ID copies of first employees
Opening quarter payroll and remuneration schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the employer file is rejected due to an inconsistent commencement date, correct the form and resubmit; a NOSI no-objection letter can be obtained where no dispute exists with prior entities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Registration and Civil Defense Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) and Civil Defense Directorate, Ministry of Interior
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the environmental registration form for a non-polluting software service facility; EEAA classification for ISIC 6201 activities is low-impact requiring only environmental registration, not a full EIA report. In parallel, schedule the fire safety inspection with the Civil Defense Directorate and obtain the workplace fire safety permit, including verification of extinguishers, exit signage, and evacuation plans.
required_dossiers: EEAA environmental registration application form
Registered office lease contract and floor plan
Civil Defense fire safety inspection request form
Declaration of no industrial wastewater or VOC emissions
Structural load clearance certificate from a licensed engineering office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If EEAA requires an environmental screening report, commission a Category-B practitioner study and resubmit within fifteen days; for Civil Defense nonconformity, install required fire suppression and exit signage and request reinspection within ten days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) and Civil Defense Directorate of the General Administration of Fire and Rescue under the Ministry of Interior; Industrial Development Authority licensing does not apply to ISIC 6201 software activities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Environmental Registration Certificate under Law 4/1994 and Civil Defense Fire Safety Permit; no separate industrial manufacturing license applies

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category (B), low environmental impact; Environmental Registration only; no Full EIA Report required for ISIC 6201 software and payroll SaaS operations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law 4/1994 as amended and Executive Regulations; wastewater discharge to public sewer per Decree 92/2013 with BOD no greater than 600 mg/L and TSS no greater than 441 mg/L; no hazardous industrial effluent or VOC emissions from office-based software operations; mandatory sound e-waste disposal and energy measurement records under EEAA registration conditions

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety approval under Civil Defense Law No. 46/1973 requiring fire extinguishers, emergency exit signage, an evacuation plan, and annual inspection; structural load clearance under the Egyptian Code of Practice ECP 201 certified by a licensed engineering firm; workplace occupational health clearance under Ministerial Decree No. 211/2003 covering working conditions and occupational safety records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – official registration portal: www.eta.gov.eg; electronic invoicing platform: portal.invoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must appoint a local fiscal representative, present incorporation documents, the parent company certificate of incorporation (apostilled), board resolution, POA, and signed EI/LI application to the Tax Account Department of the Taxpayer Services Sector. The ETA issues a unified Tax Identification Number (‘Tax Card’ / ‘Tax ID’) and VAT registration certificate. Registration is required before commencing taxable activities; the process typically takes 5–15 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; resident LLC is taxed on worldwide income; non-resident LLC is taxed on Egypt-source income only; no territorial exclusion for resident companies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists under Egyptian law. Tax consolidation is not permitted; each entity stands alone. A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC may elect to be treated as a real estate investment company (REIC) only if it meets specific real estate objects, not applicable here. No other elective entity classification mechanisms are available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 per annum of taxable turnover (goods or services).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt mandates mandatory e-invoicing under Law No. 67 of 2016 and the e-invoicing resolution. Taxable persons must transmit documents to the ETA’s e-invoice portal in real time via API (JSON format); the ETA validates and cryptographically stamps the invoice before issuance. E-receipts are also required for business-to-consumer sales. Non-compliance with e-invoicing results in rejection of deduction, fines, and escalation to mandatory reverse-charge imposition.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export applies to physical goods that leave Egypt, and to services rendered to non-resident recipients where the benefit of the service is enjoyed entirely outside Egypt (offshore services), provided the supplier retains documentary proof of export from the Egyptian customs authority and receipt of foreign currency proceeds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (certified copy from the Egyptian Customs Authority)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (or CMR for land transport) evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by an Egyptian licensed bank confirming foreign currency proceeds credited to the exporter’s account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is heavily audited. Failure to repatriate foreign exchange within the 180-day deadline or missing documentation triggers additional assessment of the 14% VAT, plus delayed tax penalty of 2% per month (or 3% for value-added tax), and a tax evasion fine of up to EGP 10 million and/or imprisonment when fraud is shown. Retrospective clawback applies for the full VAT amount plus interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) / البنك المركزي المصري - the sole monetary authority regulating banking, foreign exchange, payment systems and AML/CTF compliance in the Arab Republic of Egypt.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a unified and flexible exchange-rate regime re-established in March 2024. EGP is freely convertible for current-account transactions including software export receipts and profit remittances, subject to documentary verification by an authorized bank. Capital-account inflows are admitted only through the CBE's foreign capital registration mechanism; the inward remittance must be tied to the EG_LLC's capital file and declared in the CBE balance-of-payments return. Profit and dividend remittance require audited financial statements, an Egyptian Tax Authority tax clearance certificate, the relevant CBE purpose code, and execution at the official interbank rate. Practical hurdles include an audit trail of underlying contracts, limited onshore FX depth for large one-off remittances, and bank concentration limits for forward cover.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export receipts from software and IT services must be credited to an Egyptian licensed bank within 90 days of invoice or shipment date, in line with CBE trade-related transaction regulations; a five-month extension may apply for certain categories with prior CBE approval. The historic 100% mandatory surrender ratio has been abolished under the March 2024 liberalization. Exporters may retain and use foreign-currency receipts in CBE-licensed accounts. The bank must validate the underlying transaction through the commercial registry and e-invoice system, and the exporter must submit a monthly balance-of-payments declaration identifying realization date and currency composition.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EGP/USD current accounts; Capital Escrow Account; payroll clearing ACH sub-account
Operational EGP/USD accounts; escrowed equity injection sub-ledger; IPN payroll disbursement node
Operational multi-currency EGP/USD/EUR account; cash-sweep treasury; FX swap and deliverable forward window
Operational USD/GBP/EUR account; trade-finance disbursement sub-limits
Operational EGP/USD account; payroll treasury card and supplier payment rail

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary or sole treasury habitat for EG_LLC. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Wise, Revolut, or Payoneer cannot hold EGP, cannot settle through the CBE RTGS or Instant Payment Network, and cannot issue Egyptian IBANs; they therefore fail the statutory liquidity and audit requirements of the CBE. Locally licensed fintechs such as Fawry, Paymob, or Geidea may be used as payment-orchestration rails for payroll disbursement and domestic collections, but they must remain nested beneath a full-service CBE-licensed bank account for statutory custody, FX, and capital movements. The recommended treasury topology is to maintain the licensed bank account as the system of record and use EMIs only as niche sub-collectors for cross-border SEPA or SWIFT collections in EUR or USD, with immediate sweeping into the Egyptian account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person presence is required for first-time corporate account opening under CBE AML Law No. 80 of 2002 and the Unified AML/CTF Rules. At least two natural-person signatories, typically the Managing Director and Chief Financial Officer, must attend a branch-based KYC interview physically. For a foreign-owned EG_LLC, each foreign director must appear in person or submit a notarized and apostilled Power of Attorney appointing the Egyptian resident director or manager as the sole face-to-face representative; the POA must be legally translated into Arabic. Remote or video-KYC account opening is not recognized for corporate accounts by mainstream Egyptian banks and may be used only as an ancillary risk-mitigation step for an already low-risk customer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity where ultimate shareholders are flagged through family, shell, or multi-layer offshore structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete commercial registry extract of EG_LLC valid for thirty days; a certified beneficial-ownership declaration identifying every natural person holding at least 10% and all signatories; notarized shareholder register; FATF-compliant organisational chart showing the parent company path; and attorney-verified passport copies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or adverse-media red flags against the entity or any director due to a prior name change from 'Global Payroll Network' or a predecessor shell entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current World-Check, OFAC, EU, and UN screening report timestamped within thirty days; a board resolution attesting no sanctioned counterparties; and a legal opinion from Egyptian counsel explaining the corporate renaming and the commercial substance of EG_LLC as a payroll SaaS vendor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth insufficiency for a rapid capital injection from foreign shareholders into the capital escrow account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements for two years if available from each contributing shareholder; bank reference letter from the remitting bank with account history of at least twelve months; executed equity subscription agreement; proof of payment of applicable capital taxes; and the CBE capital-file registration receipt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cybersecurity and fiduciary risk because payroll processing aggregates personal and salary data for multiple foreign employers, raising AML/CTF third-party-payment concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISO/IEC 27001 certificate; DPIA and GDPR international transfer memorandum; a data-flow diagram demonstrating that payroll funds never traverse a pooled omnibus account and that each client payroll is masked into segregated sub-ledgers; and a signed anti-money-laundering compliance policy with risk assessment and monitoring matrix.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Purpose-code mismatch on cross-border wires where the receiving bank rejects incorrect CBE purpose codes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: E-commerce or software licensing contract and invoice tied to the exact CBE purpose code for software exports or technology services; an explanatory statement from the payment engine mapping each wire to its statutory purpose code; and a historical wire schedule evidencing consistent classification.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity proceeds must be wire-transferred via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's foreign bank to the EG_LLC's CBE-licensed beneficiary bank, identifying the beneficiary company and its Egyptian IBAN in the beneficiary field. In the remittance information field, the remitter must cite the CBE foreign-exchange purpose code for inward direct investment capital increase and reference the capital-file registration number. The Egyptian receiving bank will verify the corporate ID, the capital-increase resolution, and the ELF record before crediting the capital-escrow or operational account. Remittances above USD 100,000 trigger refreshed customer due diligence; amounts above USD 5,000,000 require a mandatory CBE balance-of-payments declaration within five business days, accompanied by proof of non-resident ownership and the CBE authorization number.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EGP disbursements for payroll automation are cleared through the CBE-operated Instant Payment Network, the Egyptian Automated Clearing House, and the RTGS large-value settlement platform. Cross-border trade settlements must be executed through SWIFT MT103 wires or documentary Commercial Letters of Credit opened for the purchasing party. The recommended treasury topology is a pooled EGP clearing account at CIB or NBE for wages, a USD disbursement account at HSBC for overseas SaaS licensing, and compliance-backed MT103 coding with the appropriate CBE business purpose code for payment for services on each outgoing wire. Outbound wires above USD 10,000 are matched against CBE reporting thresholds and relayed to the Egyptian Tax Authority e-invoice platform for digital invoice control.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EGP/USD FX forward, trade- and cash-flow-backed, CBE-authorized, with tenor up to twelve months
FX swap (EGP/USD) used as a classical spot/forward rollover for managing payroll-cycle liquidity
Cross-currency interest-rate swap (USD/EGP) requiring prior CBE approval and tied to foreign-denominated loan or creditor lines

NDF (non-deliverable forward) is not permissible for Egyptian resident corporations; the onshore regime is strictly deliverable, so an offshore NDF would require the counterparty to remain outside Egypt and would fall outside the CBE permit

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements and Auditor's Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) and the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six (6) months of fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, due by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under Articles 176 and 177 of Companies Law No. 159/1981; continued failure may result in administrative strike-off of the company's commercial registration and disqualification of managers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Tax Return (Form No. 28) with Supporting Schedules and Transfer Pricing Disclosure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four (4) months of fiscal year-end, extendable to six (6) months upon prior application; for a 31 December year-end, due 30 April (extended deadline 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 2% of the tax due per month or fraction thereof, capped, plus interest; chronic non-compliance triggers compulsory ETA assessment, collection enforcement, and criminal liability for wilful evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Assembly Resolutions and Updated Shareholder/Manager Register Extract
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: General Assembly must convene within six (6) months of fiscal year-end; resolutions and register updates must be filed within fifteen (15) days of adoption
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine not exceeding EGP 50,000, possible suspension of the commercial registration, and, if unresolved, liquidation by court order

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size-based exemption for Egyptian LLCs; every limited liability company must appoint at least one independent auditor licensed in Egypt and file audited financial statements annually. A payroll SaaS issuer with high transaction volume or cross-border payment rails must also undergo an anti-money-laundering and data-security readiness audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), substantially converged with IFRS, are mandatory for all commercial companies in Egypt; IFRS is permitted or required for listed entities and financial institutions.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A register of ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) must be maintained and submitted to GAFI; any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership must be declared within 30 days, and an annual confirmation of UBO details is required concurrently with the annual financial statements filing by 30 June.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of General Assembly Meetings
Register of Pensions and Payments (if payroll processing)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – USD 6,000 per annum for a medium-size Entity of this payroll automation business

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for payroll automation software (ISIC 6201). Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 incentives (SCZONE/free zones) and GAFI-approved deductions may apply; workforce training and R&D expenses are deductible; participation exemption may reduce residual effective tax on intercompany dividends.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 19 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed via ETA e-portal (https://portal.tax.gov.eg) by the Egyptian LLC's registered tax agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly advance CIT installments under Articles 48-49, Law 91 of 2005.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before the 4th month after fiscal year-end (December year-end: due 30 April).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: TIN, tax card, commercial registry, legal form (LLC), ISIC 6201 activity code, fiscal year period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose ultimate non-resident shareholders and ownership percentages; flag for DTA and WHT assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total SaaS subscription, implementation, and payroll-processing revenue recognized under Egyptian Accounting Standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border SaaS services used in Egypt are Egyptian-source; verify 20% WHT on applicable foreign subcontractor fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct cloud hosting, data-center, support, and sub-license costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible only with documentation and at arm's length; related-party foreign costs require TP adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Salaries, social insurance (Law 27 of 2020), training, and statutory payroll deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For foreign employees, verify tax residence certificates and 180/30-day physical-presence thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative, marketing, legal, and depreciation of software and hardware assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add-back non-deductibles: Egyptian taxes, fines, interest deemed excessive under thin-cap rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting profit to tax basis; add back non-deductibles; deduct carryforward loss (max 5 years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses cannot be surrendered to the foreign parent or used to reduce distribution obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply 22.5% CIT, deduct quarterly advance payments and creditable foreign withholding.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are unavailable for Egyptian-source income; no tax sparing relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare controlled transactions; mandatory where aggregate related-party value exceeds EGP 8,000,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Local File; attach Master File where worldwide group revenue exceeds EGP 1,000,000,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List profit distributions, applicable DTA rate, TRC status, and beneficial ownership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withhold at 10% statutory or treaty-reduced rate; follow ETA refund route if over-withheld.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: daily fine of EGP 100-200 (Article 130, Law 91/2005) capped in practice at 20% of assessed tax; late payment: non-deductible monthly delay interest under Article 127; false statements trigger criminal referral; non-filing disables ETA certificates and payment rails.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final WHT on profit distributions to shareholders (Law 91/2005, as amended).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: 1) Obtain TRC from the foreign competent authority, legalize/apostille and translate into Arabic; 2) submit TRC, beneficial-ownership declaration, and DTA application to the ETA before the first distribution; 3) obtain ETA approval for the reduced treaty rate; 4) file a refund claim through the ETA if over-withheld within the statutory limitation window (5 years).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: royalties 20%; interest 20%; technical and management fees 20%. Treaty rates commonly reduce royalties to 10-15% and interest to 10-15%; dividends range 5-15% depending on shareholding. Beneficial ownership is strictly enforced.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File trigger: aggregate controlled transactions exceeding EGP 8,000,000 per tax year; Master File trigger: MNE group consolidated revenue above EGP 1,000,000,000. Simplified TP disclosure is always required in Form 19.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: OECD hierarchical preference with ETA TP guidelines
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt has no standalone ESR regime; substance is enforced through the place-of-effective-management test (Article 3, Law 91/2005), beneficial-ownership conditions for treaty relief, and GAAR introduced under Law 25/2020. Payroll-data consistency checks by the ETA will recharacterize artificial or low-substance routing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsification of payroll records, off-book payments, under-declared SaaS revenue, forged e-invoices, and misreporting to reduce CIT and social insurance contributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 131 (Law 91/2005): imprisonment 3-5 years and/or fine EGP 20,000-50,000; recovery of evaded tax with Article 127 delay interest; seizure of bank accounts and cancellation of e-invoice registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors prosecuted jointly with the LLC; court-ordered travel bans, asset freezes, restitution orders; disqualification from GAFI and Commercial Registry positions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Egyptian LLC with no employees, no server presence, board meetings held abroad, and intercompany fee routing designed solely to minimize Egyptian CIT or claim treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR and TP recharacterization (Law 25/2020; Article 35 bis, Law 91/2005): upward TP adjustment, disallowed deductions, additional tax at 22.5% plus penal interest; denial of treaty benefits for non-beneficial owners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable where they knowingly structured sham arrangements; referral to the Public Prosecutor; corporate veil pierced on grounds of fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating payroll rails (ACH/SWIFT) without ETA AML registration, CDD/KYC on payroll beneficiaries, beneficial-owner mapping, suspicious-transaction reporting, or a compliance officer appointment (Law 80/2002, as amended by Law 36/2022).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment 3-7 years and/or fine EGP 100,000-1,000,000; legal-person fine up to EGP 10,000,000; freezing of payment-rails license and FCI authorization; enhanced de-risking by correspondent banks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members and AML compliance officer jointly and severally liable; travel bans and criminal seizure during investigations by the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Cross-Border Profit Stripping and DTA Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Reclassifying dividends as deductible royalties, management fees, or inflated interest (20% WHT) to strip Egyptian profits to low-tax jurisdictions without commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of payments, denial of deductibility, WHT at 20% plus late interest; penal assessment under Law 91/2005 Article 130; mutual agreement procedure not available once penal assessment is final.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and tax agents exposed to civil restitution and criminal complicity for signing false TP documentation; Mutual Legal Assistance requests follow the money trail.
